evidenceClassificationLegend.confirmed-by-code: Read directly from source — the strongest evidence; cites file:line
evidenceClassificationLegend.confirmed-by-code+test: Read from source AND asserted by an existing *.spec.ts/.test.ts case
evidenceClassificationLegend.confirmed-by-code+fixdoc: Read from source AND corroborated by a docs/fix/<module>/BRI-*.md point-in-time write-up
evidenceClassificationLegend.confirmed-by-code+ticket(open): Read from source; a Linear ticket describes the same behavior and is still open (tracks a known, undecided gap, not a code/ticket conflict)
evidenceClassificationLegend.confirmed-by-code+ticket(done): Read from source; a Linear ticket describes the same fix and is marked Done/QA Passed/QA Verified
evidenceClassificationLegend.gap-confirmed-by-code: A missing control/check, confirmed by reading the code (absence is the finding)
evidenceClassificationLegend.gap-confirmed-by-linear: A missing control, with a corroborating open Linear ticket
evidenceClassificationLegend.conflict: Code and a ticket/spec document disagree, or two of the knowledge base's own sources disagree — flagged, not resolved by picking one
evidenceClassificationLegend.superseded: An original spec rule was explicitly superseded by a later decision; the epic/ticket's own text says so
evidenceClassificationLegend.inferred: Not directly asserted by any single source; reasonably concluded from combining several

note: This file consolidates: (a) the 3 pre-interruption fragment files written before this session (offers, orders+disputes, payments+payment-methods+shipping — reused verbatim below, 99 rules), and (b) newly-derived entries for the remaining 28 modules, extracted from each modules/<name>.md during this session's consolidation pass. The intermediate per-batch fragments/*.json files referenced inside modules/listings.md, modules/inventory.md, modules/messaging.md, modules/notifications.md, and modules/events.md (e.g. 'see fragments/catalog-listing.business-rules.json') were never written before this session's interruption and are superseded by this single root file — do not go looking for them.

rules.rule: An offer amount must not exceed the listing price; equal-to-list is allowed.
The offer floor is seller-set (Listing.minOfferPercent) when configured, else a 50% platform default (MIN_OFFER_RATIO) — never a hard platform floor layered on top of a lower seller-set one.
Floor/ceiling checks apply identically to createOffer, createWalletHoldIntent, and a buyer's counterOffer; a seller's counter is exempt from the floor.
The negotiation window is 24h and every counter (either side) restarts the full window from its own timestamp.
rules.note: BRI-357 resolved an originally-ambiguous spec point toward 'every counter resets'.

rules.rule: Acceptance is turn-based: only the party who did not write the last history entry may accept/decline/counter; turn is derived from history, not status, and published as awaitingFrom.
rules.note: Fixes BRI-248 (seller had no action after a buyer counter-counter when clients derived turn from status alone).

rules.rule: Each party may send at most 3 counters per offer (6 rounds total); the cap blocks Counter only, not Accept/Decline.
Cancelling (withdrawing) an offer is buyer-only and not turn-based.
A seller can never offer on or accept/counter/decline their own listing's offer as the buyer.
rules.note: Offers uses 400 for this rule; OrdersService.create uses 403 for the equivalent order-side rule (BR-ORDERS-002) — same business rule, inconsistent HTTP status across modules.

rules.rule: A buyer may hold at most one open (pending/countered, unexpired) offer per listing; settled offers don't count.
Multiple buyers may hold independent open offers on the same listing; buyers never see competing offers or counts.
At most one ACCEPTED offer may exist per listing, enforced by a DB partial unique index backstopping an application check-then-write race.
rules.note: BRI-280 was the production incident that forced this to DB level.

rules.rule: Accepting an offer closes every other open/unpaid-accepted offer on the listing immediately on acceptance, not deferred to confirmed payment.
rules.note: BRI-54's original Business Rule 6 said acceptance alone does not cancel others; the epic's own 31-Aug-2026 retrospective un-ticked that criterion once the opposite shipped.

rules.rule: Acceptance commits inventory unconditionally at incrementCommitted (offers.service.ts:1124), after capture+order-creation+status-flip succeed — the earlier in-code comment 'acceptance commits no inventory' describes only the narrow concurrent-accept race window before that step is reached, not the end state.
rules.note: Resolves a contradiction flagged during this session's reconciliation pass; see modules/offers.md's Correction callout.

rules.rule: A losing buyer's notification never reveals the winning price/winner, except when the losing buyer is the winner via a different route (bought it outright).
Accept/Decline/Counter are blocked (409) once inventory is exhausted by any channel; Decline is exempt (commits nothing).
A new negotiation may only open against approved|active (narrower than checkout's active|approved|reserved); an already-open negotiation is not re-gated by listing status, only by availability.
Deleting/pausing/re-pricing-across-$2000 a listing closes every open offer, releases holds, notifies buyers; an already-accepted offer is untouched.
A block between a buyer/seller silently withdraws every open offer between that pair, with no notification.
A manual-capture payment hold is placed at offer submission, before seller response; capture happens only on accept.
Exactly one of paymentMethodId or walletPaymentIntentId must be supplied; a wallet hold is independently re-verified server-side before trust.
A counter re-authorizes a fresh hold at the new total first, cancelling the old hold only after success (card-only; wallet-originated holds cannot be re-priced).
Expiry settlement is lazy-on-read only (no scheduled sweep) — triggered only when either party opens GET /offers.
rules.note: BRI-535 open, asks for a real scheduled job.

rules.rule: A failed capture at accept time leaves the offer unchanged and returns an immediate 400 — the client's confirmed 15-min-retry-then-cancel resolution (20a) is not implemented.
rules.note: BRI-297 open; the single most consequential open gap in the module per its own epic text.

rules.rule: closeSiblingOffers (the unconditional catch-all) closes offers without releasing their Stripe holds — masked today because cancelCompetingOffers (which does release holds) already closes everything first in the single-unit-listing model.
rules.note: BRI-589 closed as 'not applicable' given single-unit listings, not fixed in code.

rules.rule: shippingCents/taxCents are snapshotted once at create/counter time and never re-read from the listing.
An accepted offer's Order is built from offer.amountCents/taxCents/shippingCents exclusively, never a live listing re-price.
An offer-created Order's payout uses the listing's locked-in commissionRateBps, never the platform's current rate at accept time.
Money is integer cents throughout every offer computation.
No admin accept/decline/counter/cancel endpoint exists for offers — admin oversight is read-only (GET /admin/offers, a separate admin-module endpoint).
An expired card cannot back a new offer/re-hold; a card with no recorded expiry (pre-dates the expiry columns) is treated as not-expired, not unknown-equals-invalid.
An unsupported card brand (e.g. UnionPay) cannot back a new offer even if saved before brand-checking existed.

OrderStatus has 8 values; seller PATCH /orders/:id/status may only advance per ALLOWED_TRANSITIONS and is restricted to SELLER_ALLOWED_STATUSES. cancelled/returned are terminal for the seller path. Admin status changes bypass this table entirely.
OrdersService.create() 403s (ForbiddenException) if any cart listing's sellerId equals the buying userId.
rules.note: BRI-72; authoritative server guard, a client-side UX gap once existed but the server was never bypassed.

rules.rule: A cart mixing listings from more than one seller is rejected with 400 before any Stripe call.
create() claims inventory atomically per item BEFORE any Stripe call (15-min hold); a real BullMQ cron (every minute) re-verifies Stripe status before releasing an expired hold.

Checkout is idempotency-keyed (userId+cart fingerprint+address+paymentMethod+10s bucket) and Order.stripePaymentIntentId carries a DB unique constraint; a P2002 returns the winning duplicate's order instead of a 500.
A Buy Now item carries expectedPriceCents; a live price mismatch at create() time is a 409. Offer-backed items are exempt (already locked).
Offer-backed pricing is snapshotted from the Offer row in both preview() and create() identically, never re-derived from the live listing.
Tax is computed once via a shared helper (calculateOrderTax) used identically by preview() and create().
Seller payout excludes tax/shipping; commission is computed per item at that item's own locked commissionRateBps, never one blended rate.

Buyer cancellation requests only succeed pre-shipment (placed|processing|packed); seller approve/deny live in sellers.controller.ts; an unanswered request auto-approves after 24h but only lazily on next read, no cron.
Seller direct cancel is immediate, no approval step; only reason=='item_unavailable' pauses the listing, 'damaged' does not.
rules.note: BRI-614 open, flags the missing confirm step and asymmetric pause.

rules.rule: Mobile hides buyer-initiated cancellation entirely (a bought order is binding by client decision); the server endpoint remains fully live and is callable only via direct API.
confirm-receipt is buyer-only, delivered-only, blocked while a non-terminal dispute is active, and uses a compare-and-set write against the 3-day lazy auto-confirm sweep (which itself has no cron).
rules.note: BRI-516 open: an order nobody opens never auto-completes.

rules.rule: A 7-day seller-never-shipped auto-cancel is lazy-on-read only, no cron.

Admin status change bypasses ALLOWED_TRANSITIONS but still writes OrderStatusHistory, stamps deliveredAt, and releases inventory correctly; admin cancelling a shipped/delivered order does not auto-refund (a separate endpoint).
rules.note: Fixes a real past inventory-leak incident where a bare admin repository write bypassed OrdersService entirely.

rules.rule: Order number is the last 8 chars of the id, upper-cased, one single source server+client.
rules.note: Fixes BRI-669/REDB1-82 (3 Seller Hub screens previously used a divergent 5-char copy).

rules.rule: Cancellation reason is a stored key (item_unavailable|damaged), not display text; buyer and seller intentionally render different wording from the identical key.
PATCH /orders/:id/status and PATCH /sellers/me/orders/:id/status both call the identical OrdersService.updateStatus with no divergence.
GET /seller/orders' status filter is an unvalidated string (not @IsEnum) — an invalid value silently matches zero rows rather than 400ing.
DisputeStatus has 7 values; server's and mobile's TERMINAL_DISPUTE_STATUSES agree exactly: denied|withdrawn|refunded are terminal, approved and refund_failed are NOT.
A claim may be opened only within 3 days of order.deliveredAt (fallback updatedAt); Dispute.orderId is @unique (one per order).
Seller evidence window is 24h; lazy-on-read advance to awaiting_decision, no cron.
Buyer evidence-add is gated to status===seller_evidence_window only.
rules.note: BRI-141 ticket open, fix already present in code.

rules.rule: Seller submitting evidence unconditionally flips status to awaiting_decision (no window-status gate beyond !decidedAt).
Seller 'accept return' is the identical internal code path as an admin approval.
Decision (approve/deny) is claimed atomically (updateMany WHERE decidedAt IS NULL), preventing a double-click or accept/approve race from buying two return labels.

A genuine Shippo label-purchase failure now throws ServiceUnavailableException (503) instead of silently faking a label; the mock fallback is only used for genuinely-not-attempted cases (missing dimensions/address/profile, over-cap parcel).
rules.note: BRI-414 fix; BRI-657 open re: no retry affordance in the mobile UI for the resulting 503.

rules.rule: The refund trigger (triggerReturnRefund) is atomically claimed (returnShippedAt CAS) and shared by buyer self-report and real carrier-tracking/webhook.

A buyer's manual 'I've shipped it' tap refunds immediately with no carrier verification, for any dispute whose label fell back to mock — true for every real-world dispute today since no listing carries package dimensions.
The 5-day return-ship window auto-releases the payout hold (lazy, no cron) without resolving the dispute — status stays 'approved' indefinitely until a late ship.
refund_failed is a dead-end queryable state with no retry endpoint/sweep/admin action found anywhere in the module.
refundOrder blocks on an open genuine StripeDispute (chargeback), deliberately not on Dispute.payoutHeld (which the internal flow sets true on itself mid-refund).
Opening a dispute is not blocked by a prior buyer receipt confirmation — confirmReceipt never changes order.status off 'delivered'.
The seller is never notified of claim approve/deny/refund outcomes — only the buyer, across all three resolution paths.
The mobile DisputeStatus screen has no explicit branch for refund_failed — falls through to the generic 'Under review' branch which renders a Withdraw button the server will reject.
The admin dispute-case queue (GET /admin/dispute-cases) excludes 'approved' by design — a stuck approved-but-unshipped case is only reachable by a direct by-id lookup.
The internal Dispute model and the StripeDispute (chargeback) model are independent and can both exist simultaneously on one order.
ReportDisputeDto.description accepts an empty string (no @IsNotEmpty despite being nominally required).
POST /payments/webhook requires the raw body + a stripe-signature header verified via constructEvent; an invalid signature is 400.
Webhook deliveries dedupe by Stripe event id via an atomic upsert; a 'processed' row skips re-running; 'failed'/fresh rows are (re)processed.
Any thrown handler error marks the event 'failed' and rethrows to produce a 500, the intended Stripe-retry signal.
payment_intent.succeeded with no matching Order throws deliberately so Stripe retries until the Order row is queryable.
payment_intent.payment_failed/.canceled with no matching Order is a silent, expected no-op (offer-hold PaymentIntents never had an Order).
A webhook-amount vs Order.total mismatch is logged at error but never blocks recording the payment as succeeded.
charge.refunded is a no-op if Payment already refunded; full-vs-partial is derived from cumulative amount_refunded, tax reversal sized to the increment only.
charge.dispute.*/transfer.* events are dispatched to ConnectService, not handled in this module.
refundOrderPayment only acts on succeeded|partially_refunded, caps to remaining unrefunded balance, maps client-cause Stripe errors to 400.

Idempotency — Stripe-operation level: every retryable Stripe-side write (customer/account creation, transfer, refund, tax transaction/reversal, checkout PaymentIntent, offer holds) carries a deterministic idempotencyKey scoped to the operation+order/event. This is closed and unit-tested, distinct from the genuinely-absent generic API-request-level idempotency (no Idempotency-Key header/middleware exists anywhere) — see overview.md's corrected idempotency section.
A sibling raw-body route /payments/webhook/connect exists under ConnectModule and shares the same WebhookEvent dedup table.
All 3 endpoints require JwtAuthGuard at class level — no public routes.
Attach is idempotent two ways: exact Stripe id already saved, or a different id but same physical card (brand+last4+exp) already saved — both return alreadySaved:true, no duplicate row.
Only visa/mastercard/amex/discover may be saved; a refused brand is attached-then-detached (to learn the brand) and rejected with 400.
A stale/cross-environment Stripe customer id triggers exactly one recreate-and-retry before failing.
Delete is ownership-checked (403) and blocked (409) if the card backs an open unexpired offer hold, checked before any Stripe call.
Delete is a hard delete at both Stripe and the local row; Orders/Offers snapshot cardBrand/cardLast4 at creation so a later deletion never corrupts past-order display.
PaymentMethod.isDefault exists in schema/DTO and drives sort order, but no code path ever sets it true — dead field, findAll is always newest-first in practice.

Attach-idempotency is an application-level findFirst check with no DB unique constraint — two concurrent identical POSTs can both pass and insert two rows; pre-existing duplicate rows in the shared DB were never cleaned up pending sign-off.
A row detached from Stripe out-of-band (Dashboard/expiry) is never revalidated — GET keeps listing it; the failure surfaces only at checkout as a raw Stripe error.
rules.note: REDB1-124/BRI-823; fix boundary is orders.service.ts, not this module.

rules.rule: No server-side notion of 'why this card is being added' (checkout vs offer-gate) exists — that context lives entirely in mobile React-Navigation route params (BRI-268's fix was frontend-only). No API test can exercise this distinction.
GET /shipping/tiers is public by design so it works before seller confirmation.
The 4 shipping tiers are hard-coded constants, not DB-driven/admin-configurable; a prior ShippingConfig table was deliberately removed.
Tier prices/weight bands are the single source of truth also consumed by ai/shippability.ts and by mobile+web — must never be independently re-declared.
POST /shipping/webhook/shippo is a pure no-op unless SHIPPO_TRACKING_MODE=webhook; polling is the documented production default and no signature verification runs in non-webhook mode.
HMAC (shippo-auth-signature) takes precedence over a URL ?token= when both configured; boot fails if webhook mode is set with neither secret configured.
If neither secret is configured the handler fails OPEN (warns, accepts unauthenticated) — reachable only via a dev boot bypassing env validation.
The webhook resolves 200 for every safe-to-ignore case, 400/401 for a payload/auth problem Shippo shouldn't retry, and lets a genuine error propagate to 500 (Shippo retries).
(carrier, trackingNumber) has no DB uniqueness; an ambiguous match resolves to the most-recently-created row, logged at error for manual investigation.
Inbound webhook fields are read defensively in both snake_case and camelCase since the exact wire shape was never confirmed against a real Shippo delivery.
A resolved tracking update emits an event (EventEmitter2), not a direct call into Orders/Disputes, to avoid a module cycle; the consuming status-transition logic lives in orders/disputes.
Shipment.labelUrl/qrCodeUrl are long-lived (~1yr), unauthenticated bearer links to Shippo-hosted PDFs containing shipping PII.
rules.note: BRI-848, Todo, MobSF dynamic security finding.

rules.rule: Signup email must not already belong to a user; 409 'You have already signed up. Please sign in.'
Signup username must be available (409 USERNAME_TAKEN); no disambiguation/suffix — honored exactly or refused.
Login: a missing user and a wrong password are both the identical 401 'Invalid credentials.' — no email-enumeration via error text.
A suspended user is refused login (401 'Account suspended.'), checked after the credential check.
A successful login via email/password, OTP-verify, or Google cancels a pending account deletion if one is scheduled (cancelPendingDeletionOnLogin); failure here is swallowed.

forgot-password always returns the same success message regardless of whether the email exists (anti-enumeration); the reset OTP is stored as PLAINTEXT on User.resetToken (unlike every other OTP flow, which stores a bcrypt hash).
OTP sign-in request checks an email-scoped lockout (OtpLockout) FIRST, before issuing a new code — closes the hole where a fresh code reset the attempt counter.
OTP resend is capped at 3 per code cycle; the 4th request starts a 15-minute cooldown (429 OTP_COOLDOWN).
The OTP TTL is 1 minute (OTP_TTL_MS), restamped from mint-time to send-time so a slow SMTP relay doesn't eat the window before the user sees the code.
OTP verify: 5 wrong attempts deletes the code row (invalidated, not just blocked) and escalates OtpLockout (15min base, doubling to 24h max); a correct code clears the escalating counter to zero.

A fresh account created via OTP-verify gets a random unusable password hash and a username either honored exactly (re-validated) or auto-derived; zip/ageBracket/gender persist only on create, never overwriting a returning user.

Social sign-in (Google/Apple/Facebook) requires the provider's own 'sign_in_provider'/equivalent claim to match, and refuses (409) rather than silently linking if the email already belongs to a different, non-socially-linked account.
rules.note: BRI-648 Backlog is a product-scoped limitation per this rule, not a bug.

rules.rule: A brand-new Google account requires Firebase's emailVerified claim true; an unverified email is refused, not trusted.

loginWithApple and loginWithFacebook never call cancelPendingDeletionOnLogin for an existing non-suspended user — unlike login/OTP-verify/Google, so a deleted-then-signs-back-in-via-Apple-or-Facebook user does NOT get their deletion auto-cancelled.
rules.note: Real, unticketed correctness gap — BRI-375's restore-on-login is only honored for email/OTP/Google.

rules.rule: Seller OTP sign-in (otp/seller/request) only emails a code if user.isSeller && !suspended, but ALWAYS returns 200 unconditionally — including lockout/cooldown, which are swallowed (logged only) to prevent fingerprinting which emails are seller accounts. The buyer OTP twin DOES throw 429 for lockout/cooldown.

Seller OTP verify never creates an account (401 'This email isn't a registered seller account.' if no user/not a seller) and uses the LEGACY long-lived token (bypassing issueSession/BRI-334 rotation) — no sid, not listable/revocable via the sessions endpoints.

GET /auth/dev/otp and GET /users/me/deletion/dev-code both 404 unconditionally when NODE_ENV===production, checked before the service runs — same environment-only gate pattern used by seed/embeddings.
refresh-claims re-mints an access token with current DB claims, preserving the caller's sid; it is NOT the refresh-token exchange and issues no new refresh token.
Refresh-token reuse detection: a replayed already-revoked token revokes the ENTIRE rotation family and 401s; ordinary expiry (not-yet-revoked, just past expiresAt) does not trigger family revocation.
Refresh rotation (create new row + mark old revoked/replacedById) happens in one $transaction; new refresh-token expiry is always a rolling now+90 days, not counted from original issuance.

Logout requires no auth at the HTTP layer (works against an already-expired access token) and revokes the WHOLE rotation family of the presented refresh token, not just the one row; malformed/unmatched tokens are a silent no-op.
GET /auth/sessions lists one row per live rotation family for the caller; a legacy/admin token (no sid) lists nothing even though the caller IS authenticated via it.
revoke-others requires req.user.sid; a pre-BRI-454 token with no sid is refused (400) rather than guessed at, since revoking everything would also sign the caller out.
DELETE /auth/sessions/:id scopes the revoke to the caller's own userId — another user's familyId is indistinguishable from unknown (both 404, never 403).
change-password requires the current password to match (401 otherwise); on success it also clears any stray resetToken and does NOT revoke other devices' refresh-token sessions.
rules.note: Same gap as reset-password: a stolen-then-changed password doesn't force other devices to re-authenticate.

rules.rule: Password reset (via the legacy OTP flow) does not revoke existing refresh-token sessions either — every other signed-in device stays alive.

verify-current-password returns {valid:boolean} rather than throwing — a UX pre-check only, never the actual authorization gate for anything; it is throttled specifically because it would otherwise be an unlimited-guess password oracle.

@Throttle(STRICT)=10/min/IP applies to every auth route except refresh-claims and logout; two session models coexist (90-day rolling refresh-token for real sign-ins, legacy long-lived single token for ADMIN sessions and web seller OTP login).

sellerStatus ('none'|'pending'|'active') is derived identically in UsersService.toSafeUser and AuthService.sellerStatusOf; mobile's utils/sellerState.ts mirrors it a third time and additionally defines a client-only 'verifying' status the server never sends.

PATCH /users/me: username is optional (omitting leaves it untouched, conflict-checked only when present); phone uses trim()||null (empty string explicitly clears it) while every other optional field uses ??null (omission leaves it alone) — two different null-vs-omit semantics on the same DTO.
ageBracket/gender/dateOfBirth are written only when present in the body (conditional-spread) — a profile save that doesn't touch them never wipes a signup-captured value.
dateOfBirth is captured (custom validator) but NOT enforced as an under-18 financial-agreement block anywhere in this module.
rules.note: REDB1-146, Todo — matches the DTO's own comment exactly.

rules.rule: PATCH /users/me/preferences: only a real shopping-facet (categories/sizes/brands/styles, non-empty) clears prefsSkipped to false; saving personalizedRecommendations or notifications alone does not.
notifications merge-not-replace: only keys present+boolean in the incoming body overwrite the saved prefs; every omitted key is preserved from the current row.
A changed notifications.marketing value fires a fire-and-forget Mailchimp subscribe/unsubscribe AFTER the DB write; a no-op re-save of the same value never re-triggers it; failure never surfaces.
BRI-521 shows Reopened in Linear even though the merge logic is present and unit-tested in code — evidence conflict, flag for runtime verification rather than assuming either source alone.
Registering a push token also detaches that same token from every OTHER account currently holding it, atomically — a token identifies a device, not an account.
POST /users/me/active stamps lastActiveAt and is called only on app foreground/resume, not every request.

Deletion eligibility blockers are computed live, never cached: activeOrders (buyer OR seller side, 5 blocking statuses), pendingPayouts, openDisputes (approved still blocks since refund hasn't issued); windowDays is 30, or 60 if there's been financial activity in the last 30 days.

Deletion request re-checks blockers (not trusted from a prior eligibility read), 409s if already scheduled, and AWAITS the confirmation email send (a mail failure surfaces as a real error) — unlike every OTP email elsewhere, which is fire-and-forget.

Deletion confirm has NO attempt-lockout on the 6-digit code (contrast the sign-in OTP's 5-attempt lockout) — rate-limited only by the global 100/min default, since this controller has no @Throttle decorators.
Deletion confirm re-checks blockers a THIRD time immediately before the write, and burns the code in the same write that schedules deletion (can't replay).

DELETE /users/me/deletion (cancel) exists, is a safe no-op against nothing-scheduled, and cannot resurrect an already-purged account — but no mobile UI reaches it; the actual used cancel path is the automatic one inside every sign-in method except Apple/Facebook.
GET /users/sellers excludes the caller and requires sign-in even though it's a discovery endpoint; search strips a leading @ since username is stored without it.

GET /users/:id is public and does NOT 403/404 a suspended account — the DTO includes isSuspended so the client decides what to render; contrast the follow endpoint, which treats a suspended target as not-found.

GET /users/:id/listings has a confirmed duplicate-surface gap: the shipped mobile ShopProfile screen instead calls GET /listings?sellerId=... (a different, listings-module endpoint) — this dedicated route appears unused by either frontend.
GET /users/:id/likes enforces both auth (401) and ownership (403, requesterId!==userId) — fixed from a historical no-guard-at-all bug.

POST /users/:id/follow: self-follow 400; a suspended or nonexistent target is 404 (not 403, to avoid confirming existence); target must be a confirmed seller (400 otherwise); a buyer who has hidden the seller cannot follow (400) until unhidden; already-following is 409; follow takes effect immediately with no seller-approval step.
rules.note: BRI-65/95/468/461/470 — all confirmed fixed in code; Linear shows BRI-461/468 still 'QA Testing' (code-fixed, pending tracker closure, not a conflict).

rules.rule: Follow/unfollow's mobile client (followsStore.toggle()) has NO pendingSync serialization chain against rapid-tap races — the identical shape as the already-fixed likesStore race (BRI-290), confirmed unpatched by reading the full file.
rules.note: apps/mobile/CLAUDE.md explicitly calls this out as a documented, not-yet-applied fix under BRI-95.

rules.rule: POST /users/:id/report is a genuine, real endpoint (creates a UserReport row) but the mobile seller-shop-page 'Report' UI shows a success toast WITHOUT making any network call — a silent false-success UX bug. Only the web seller-portal caller (reporting a follower/reviewer) actually hits this endpoint.
GET /sellers/me/commission-rate returns the platform's CURRENT rate — never an existing listing/order's own locked-in rate (which lives on those rows directly).

GET /sellers/check-shop-name has no excludeUserId support — a seller re-checking their OWN current/similar shop name gets reason:'taken' against themselves; SellersService.apply() DOES pass excludeUserId at actual submission.
Phone OTP has a hardcoded QA test-number bypass (+12264550694 -> fixed code 000000) gated additionally on NODE_ENV!==production.

POST /sellers/apply requires phoneVerifiedNumber to exactly E.164-match the submitted number AND phoneVerifiedAt within 30 minutes; the whole DTO is class-level address-consistency-validated before Shippo is ever called; a Shippo 'undeliverable' verdict blocks (400), a Shippo outage fails OPEN.
Seller activation (isSeller:true) is instant on a successful apply() — no email-confirmation step, no Stripe Connect requirement; isSeller and Stripe payout-verification are independent gates.
No age/date-of-birth gate exists anywhere in ApplySellerDto/SellersService.apply for the Tax ID step, despite a PRD requirement for an under-18 block on financial agreements.
A seller's taxId raw value is never persisted/logged/returned — only its last-4 digits are stored.
GET /sellers/me's bank payout field is a last-4 summary only — no endpoint in this module ever exposes full account/routing numbers.

Shipping order stats' cancellationRate counts ONLY seller-attributable cancellations (prefix-matched on the status-history description) — a buyer-requested-and-approved cancellation never counts, even though the seller clicked approve.

GET /sellers/me/orders/chart buckets 'day' using LOCAL server time zone consistently on both sides of the comparison — a past bug class (desyncing 'Today' by a day on a non-UTC server) is now guarded.
GET /sellers/me/orders/:id has a side effect on read: maybeAutoApproveCancellation can mutate order status as part of a GET if a pending request exceeded its 24h window.

shipOrder NEVER re-purchases a label already bought via the dedicated Buy-Shipping-Label flow; auto-purchase is attempted only when every precondition (dimensions, addresses, weight cap) is met, otherwise it silently falls back to client-supplied tracking rather than erroring; a genuine Shippo API failure (as opposed to missing preconditions) is a hard 503 + admin alert.
rules.note: Fixes a real 2026-09-14 carrier-choice production bug.

rules.rule: A label-purchase claim (claimForPurchase) is atomic — a double-tap/retry either returns the existing label ('already_purchased') or 409s ('in_progress'), never buys a second real label; the claim is released on any failure path.

PATCH /sellers/me/orders/:id/ship bypasses OrdersService.updateStatus's own state machine entirely (writes status:'shipped' via its own repository call) and must independently fire the buyer 'Order Shipped' notification itself.
purchaseShippingLabel refuses a cross-order rate reuse (400) — a rateId quoted for order A cannot purchase a label against order B.

GET /sellers/me/orders/:id's ownership-mismatch error (flat 404) is INCONSISTENT with PATCH .../status's ownership-mismatch error (403) for the identical kind of violation within the same controller — a real information-disclosure asymmetry (403 confirms the order exists, 404 doesn't).

GET /sellers/me/listings' status filter is a raw ListingStatus value, deliberately NOT the same grouping as the mobile Seller Hub's own tabs (e.g. status=active misses approved/reserved) — the mobile client has no wrapper for this endpoint for exactly this reason, using a different listings-module endpoint instead for tab-shaped views.
A pause->reactivate cycle (PATCH .../listings/:id/status) never re-locks the commission rate; only a true relist (via createListing) picks up a fresh platform rate.

UpdateOrderStatusDto.trackingUrl (orders module, used by PATCH .../status) is @IsUrl-validated; ShipOrderDto.trackingUrl (sellers module, used by the dedicated ship endpoint) is a plain unvalidated string — two different strictness levels for the conceptually-same field, both ultimately writing Order.trackingUrl.
GET /sellers/me/customers has no pagination/date filter — aggregates over ALL of the seller's orders in memory, including cancelled-order totals.

POST /sellers/connect/onboard is idempotent: an existing ConnectAccount is returned as-is; a race on the unique userId constraint is caught (P2002) and the loser re-reads the winner's row; the Stripe call itself carries its own idempotency key.
onboard sweeps every pre-existing payable order for the new account (sweepPendingOrdersForNewAccount) best-effort — a failure here never fails the onboard call itself.

A local-write 500 AFTER a successful Stripe account creation is a real, non-idempotent-from-the-client's-view failure: a client retry would create a SECOND Stripe account unless the first local write eventually lands.
GET /sellers/connect/status with no ConnectAccount returns a 200 all-false/{exists:false} shape, never a 404 — callers must branch on exists.

getStatus has a real write side effect on every GET: retryFailedPayouts runs unconditionally, and a stale (>1h) or force:true unverified row triggers a live Stripe reconciliation that updates local state and fires notifications on a restricted/rejected transition.

force:true exists specifically because onboarding completes Stripe verification in the same session, making the row always 'too fresh' to trip the normal 1-hour staleness check; onboarding passes force:true, Settings' payout screen does not.

accountStatus derivation: a disabledReason starting 'rejected.' always wins as 'rejected'; else !payoutsEnabled && pastDue.length>0 is 'restricted' (keyed on past_due specifically, not currently_due); else payoutsEnabled?'verified':'pending'. 'deauthorized' is never derived, only ever written directly by the deauthorization webhook handler.

POST /sellers/connect/account-session/payout requires phoneVerifiedAt within 5 minutes (tighter than apply()'s 30-minute window, since this gates an active bank-detail change) — or an admin-set phone2faOverrideUntil still in the future.
POST /payments/webhook/connect has zero NestJS guards — auth is entirely the Stripe HMAC signature check inside the service; a bad/missing signature is 400, not 401/403.

charge.dispute.*/transfer.* are deliberately NOT dispatched via the connect-scoped webhook — under Separate Charges & Transfers, Stripe never delivers those event types to a connect:true endpoint; they arrive via the platform /payments/webhook instead, calling the same ConnectService handler methods from a different controller.

transferForOrder requires deliveredAt set AND a 3-day hold window elapsed (STRIPE_CONNECT_TRANSFER_TIMING default) before transferring; not payoutsEnabled writes Payout.status='held_unverified' rather than failing; already-transferred is a no-op; no ConnectAccount at all leaves nothing written (picked up later by the onboard sweep).

refundOrder reverses any already-transferred payout TWICE (once up front, once immediately before the Stripe refund call) to close a race window; a reversal failure records Payout.status='reversal_failed', alerts every admin, and BLOCKS the refund entirely rather than refunding while leaving the seller's transfer un-reversed.
Payout.reversedAmount is cumulative; a partial reversal does NOT flip status to 'reversed' until the running total reaches the full amount.

account.application.deauthorized sets chargesEnabled/payoutsEnabled false, accountStatus='deauthorized', and alerts EVERY admin in-app only (no email channel for this one event, unlike restricted/rejected which get both).

REDB1-48/BRI-786 is Reopened: the exact scenario getStatus's force flag was built to fix (first-time seller cannot continue after Stripe verification) is back, meaning the original fix regressed or is incomplete.

No class-level guard on ListingsController — most routes are public; auth applied per-route. Route-ordering is verified safe (literal-segment paths declared before :id, segment-count disambiguation confirmed correct by Express/Nest matching).

The buyer-facing DTO flattens lifecycle status to status:'available'|'sold'|'reserved' (mapStatus treats draft/pending_approval/rejected/inactive all as 'available') AND separately returns the full listingStatus field — the latter is the only authoritative 'is this live' field; a client reading only status sees a paused/draft/rejected listing as available.

createListing: brandId is required; price>=highValueThresholdCents (default $2000) forces pending_approval unless the client explicitly requested draft; prohibited-content screening and photo weapon/blur screening both run server-side and fail closed (500, nothing saved) if the screen itself is down.

deleteListing (soft delete): blocked (409) by any order item OR an accepted offer on the listing; every open offer is explicitly cancelled with holds released before the delete, count returned as offersCancelled.

relistListing only refuses status==='draft' — it does NOT require 'sold'; a live/paused listing can be relisted as a full duplicate while the original is left untouched, so an item can be listed twice simultaneously. Client and server agree on this (wrong, per spec) behavior.

updateListingStatus performs NO transition-table validation at all — any of the 8 enum values is accepted and written as-is; only the 'pause' case (approved/active -> inactive/draft) triggers the offer-cancellation side effect. A seller can self-approve a pending_approval listing via this route, bypassing the admin-only /approve endpoint's role guard entirely.
rules.note: Currently only exploitable via a direct API call — no shipped mobile UI path sends sold/approved/rejected/reserved.

rules.rule: updateListing hard-blocks any edit on status==='sold' (409) before any other validation; category/subcategory/type are validated against the listing's state AFTER the edit applies, as a unit.

A price edit crossing UPWARD over the high-value threshold while live demotes to pending_approval and cancels open offers; crossing back DOWNWARD while pending_approval with a prior approvedAt auto-restores to approved with no second admin pass. An edit not touching price never re-evaluates the threshold.

Photo re-screening on update re-runs whenever the final photo-SET COMPOSITION changes at all (added or removed), not merely on new-photo-add, since a photo can read differently once a companion photo is removed.
Sending attributes on update REPLACES the whole set; moving to a different subcategory/type without resending attributes silently clears old answers (logged, not surfaced to the client).
approve/reject require the real Role.ADMIN enum (not 'SELLER'); reject requires a mandatory 5-500 char reason at the DTO boundary.

GET /listings excludes the viewer's own listings and any seller they've hidden, UNLESS an explicit sellerId is passed (a directed shop-view always wins over undirected-discovery exclusion); status=sold is only valid together with sellerId.
sort=trending ranks by ListingEvent view-count in the last 72h, excluding listings newer than 2h so an early view can't top the rail.

The hybrid search leg (keyword + text-embedding fusion by reciprocal rank) degrades to keyword-only on any provider/Qdrant failure, never 500ing the whole search; partialMatches (semantic/synonym-only hits) are page-1-only and never merged into the primary data array.
GET /listings/price-bounds explicitly ignores any incoming minPrice/maxPrice — the bounds describe the full choosable range, never the range already chosen.

Visual search empties the whole result set below a 0.70 close-match floor (rather than showing noise), with explicit safeguards keeping an exact-match (score>=0.9) row regardless of taxonomy mismatch, and a catalogCoverage field distinguishing 'nothing matched' from 'we don't carry this category'.
search/text-semantic-preview has NO guard decorator at all — gated only by a runtime NODE_ENV==='production' check (404s in prod, reachable unauthenticated in dev/staging).

GET /listings/mine's status filter maps a 5-value UI enum to real ListingStatus arrays via MY_LISTINGS_STATUSES (active includes reserved, so an accepted-offer-pending-payment listing shows under Active, not invisible).

GET /listings/:id/open-offers mirrors deleteListing's exact 409 conditions (blockedReason: 'order' wins over 'accepted_offer') so the seller's delete-confirm dialog can warn accurately before committing.

GET /listings/:id's cache (listing:<id>, no per-identity variant) runs the visibility gate AFTER the cache read, per request — only pending_approval 404s for anyone but the owner/admin; draft/rejected/inactive/sold/reserved remain reachable via direct GET (supporting stale deep-links with disabled CTAs).

Every write path that changes a listing's detail-page response must call invalidateCache — a past admin take-down path once skipped this and showed a stale ACTIVE detail page for ~15s (BRI-438, fixed; flagged as a pattern any NEW write path must remember).

GET /listings/:id/likes 404s on an unknown listing id (not an empty array) — 'no likes' and 'bad id' must not read the same; GET /listings/:id/comments has NO such existence check and returns [] either way — an inconsistency between two otherwise-parallel endpoints.

likeListing 404s for a listing in NON_LIKEABLE_LISTING_STATUSES (draft/pending_approval/rejected/inactive) and 403s the listing's own seller (self-like); sold/reserved are deliberately left likeable (an explicitly undecided product question in the code's own comment).

Like/unlike have no server-side serialization across a rapid like->unlike->like sequence from one user — correctness for that race lives entirely in the mobile client's pendingSync chain (BRI-290); a second client (web/script) hitting this endpoint directly is exposed to the same race server-side.

addComment has NO status gate at all (unlike likeListing) and NO self-comment restriction — a buyer with a leaked/guessed pending_approval listing id can comment on a listing GET /listings/:id itself refuses to show them; the listing's own seller can comment on their own listing.
rules.note: Asymmetry with the like endpoint's moderation posture, not confirmed exploited by any ticket.

rules.rule: Self-exclusion on engagement signals is uniform: a seller's own presence heartbeat is a silent no-op, and self-views are excluded at write time by EventsService.screen (events module) — neither Views nor Watchers can be inflated by the owner checking their own listing.

available is never stored, always derived as max(0, onHand-committed-unavailable); a Listing with no Inventory row yet falls back to Listing.stock as effective onHand until the first mutation seeds a real row via upsert.

The 4 mutation primitives (incrementCommitted/decrementCommitted/commitForReservation/decrementOnHand) are NOT exposed by this controller's 4 endpoints at all — they're called only from offers/orders; this module's PUT only ever calls upsertAvailable (a manual-edit path).

GET /seller/inventory/listings/:listingId and its PUT/history siblings use a plain findFirst with NO soft-delete filter (unlike the listings module's findByIdForOwner) — a soft-deleted listing's inventory remains readable/writable through this endpoint even though it's invisible everywhere else.

GET /seller/inventory (list) runs a self-healing read: any row where available>0 AND listing.status==='sold' (drift state) is batch-flipped back to 'active' as a side effect of the GET, syncing the embedding index for each flipped row — a deliberate repair-on-read, not accidental.

UpdateInventoryDto clamps any non-numeric/negative input to 0 via a @Transform BEFORE class-validator runs — the '400 must be an integer' path is effectively unreachable; bad input silently becomes a 200 with onHand recomputed as if 0 was sent.

PUT's write formula: newOnHand = quantityAvailable + committed + unavailable (seller edits AVAILABLE, server back-solves onHand); committed/unavailable are left exactly as they were — a seller cannot free a held unit through this endpoint.

The entire PUT write (read oldAvailable, upsert onHand, conditionally flip Listing.status, write one history row) is one $transaction; status auto-flip only covers active/approved<->sold — 'reserved' is never auto-flipped by this path.

A past production incident (manual-sql 2026-08-31) occurred entirely in a BYPASSED admin order-write path (not this module's own endpoints) — three admin routes used to write Order.status directly, skipping decrementOnHand/decrementCommitted, leaving committed held forever against a concluded sale.

decrementCommitted/decrementOnHand now floor at 0 directly inside the raw UPDATE statement via GREATEST(...,0) — chosen over a read-then-floor-in-JS approach specifically to preserve atomicity under concurrent releases.
No pagination at all on GET .../history (unbounded findMany) — low risk today (manual edits are infrequent) but a latent gap if adjustment frequency increases.

Web's getInventory/getListingInventoryHistory client methods are defined but have no caller anywhere outside sellerApi.ts itself — the standalone seller Inventory page was removed from web's routing; these 2 of 4 endpoints are reachable only by direct API call today.
createConversation requires at least one of sellerId/listingId (conditionally-required, not a bare @IsNotEmpty on either); fixes BRI-498.

createConversation 403s a caller who is chat-banned or trying to message about their own listing; the caller is always the buyer side of a new thread — only createConversationAsSeller (the order-anchored route) can make a seller the originator.
createConversation performs NO block check at all — a blocked pair can still create a new conversation row.

createConversation is idempotent: non-null listingId upserts on the composite unique; null listingId uses findFirst-then-create with P2002-catch-and-refetch (Postgres treats composite-unique NULLs as distinct rows, so a naive upsert alone would duplicate).

GET /conversations/:id has a SECOND, less-restricted authorization path: any ADMIN JWT can read it even without going through the dedicated admin controller — participant-or-admin, not participant-only.
GET /conversations/:id/messages is participant-ONLY — unlike its sibling GET /conversations/:id, it has no admin role-bypass; an admin must use the dedicated admin route instead.

sendMessage checks both block directions separately (403 BLOCKED_BY_ME if caller blocked recipient; 403 RECIPIENT_BLOCKED if recipient blocked caller) so the message text never reveals who blocked whom.

classify(body): payment/contact content is hard-blocked (403, never persisted); any other flag (profanity, bare URL) does NOT block — the message is created with isFlagged:true and delivered normally.

A sent message always writes a Notification row (never skipped); only the PUSH is conditionally suppressed when the recipient is actively viewing the conversation (isUserActiveOnConversation) — the in-app record is never skipped.

Only buyers can attach a listing/order reference (resolveReferences) — a seller attempting to attach one is 403'd; the referenced listing must belong to the conversation's seller, the referenced order to the conversation's buyer+seller pair.

markRead is conversation READ-STATE only — distinct from and non-interacting with notification read-state (Notification.read). Mobile's Messages-tab badge and Offers-tab dot deliberately read two different underlying data sources for exactly this reason.
reportConversation rate-limits to one OPEN report per reporter-per-conversation (400 on a second attempt while the first is unresolved) — not a time-window limit.

DELETE /conversations/:id is a per-user soft delete (deletedByBuyer/deletedBySeller) — the other participant's view is completely unaffected; a new message in the thread resets BOTH flags to false, resurfacing a hidden thread for whichever side had hidden it.

blockFromConversation derives context (buyer/seller) from the caller's own role in THIS conversation with no client input; it ALSO silently cancels every open offer between the pair, with no notification to the other side (per code comment: no money has moved, safe to withdraw silently).

POST /me/blocked-users/:userId requires context explicitly (unlike in-conversation block, which derives it) since there's no conversation to infer it from; also cancels open offers, and unfollows the blocked seller if context==='buyer' and currently followed.
unblockUser is one-way (lifts only the caller's own block, 404 if none exists) and restores every shared conversation hidden by that side's block.
Admin's JWT role claim is checked DIRECTLY (not a live DB re-check) — an admin's access is only as fresh as their last token issue, unlike 'SELLER' checks elsewhere which are always live-DB.

GET /admin/conversations/:id/messages reuses shapeMessage, which does NOT special-case deletedAt — the admin UI must separately decide whether to show the real body or honor deletedAt itself; not independently verified in the web page which it does.
adminRemoveMessage is a soft delete only, 404 if missing, 400 if already removed (no double-remove, no un-remove path).

resolveReport's targetUserId is admin-supplied and TRUSTED AS-IS with no server-side validation that it's actually a participant in the conversation — the web UI defaults it sensibly but the API itself doesn't enforce it.

resolveReport's 'warn' auto-escalates to a 100-year ban + a second system message once chatWarningCount reaches 3; 'ban' with lockConversation ALSO sets status=admin_locked + a third system message; lockConversation is silently ignored for warn/suspend/dismiss.
Every moderation system message is visible to BOTH participants (not addressed to just the target), so ban/warn/suspend copy reads oddly to the OTHER participant too.
No action in resolveReport or adminChatBan ever notifies the targeted user — they only discover it via a failed message send or by reading a system message if present in the thread.

POST /admin/users/:id/chat-ban is a direct chatBanUntil write with NO conversation context, no system message, no notification, and no report interaction — a materially different, simpler path than resolveReport despite similar-looking web UI buttons.
GET /me/conversations resolves a 'latest referenced listing' per row via one extra batched query (not one query per row) and surfaces it in the listing field.
GET /admin/conversation-reports has NO pagination at all — returns the full matching set, a scale risk if report volume grows, unlike every other admin list route in the module.

The two WebSocket gateways (MessagingGateway /ws/chat, RealtimeGateway /ws/user) are fully independent namespaces with no shared state; MessagingGateway has NO client->server message-send event — HTTP POST is the only write path, the gateway is push-only for content.
Both gateways fail CLOSED on JWT misconfiguration/invalid token (disconnect, logged), never accepting an unauthenticated socket.

isUserActiveOnConversation considers a user active if focused on the conversation OR their last socket disconnected within the last 15s without an explicit blur since — a reconnect/transport-blip grace window used exclusively to gate push suppression, never the DB notification record.

Review (seller/transaction rating, @@unique[reviewerId,orderId]) and ProductReview (per-listing rating, @@unique[reviewerId,listingId]) are two genuinely independent rows, both written by one POST /orders/:id/review call in one $transaction.
submitOrderReview's only time/lifecycle check is order.status==='delivered' — no comparison against deliveredAt/receiptConfirmedAt/any elapsed-time field.
rules.note: BRI-96 states a confirmed '7-day window after order completion' business rule the code does not enforce at all — a genuine spec-vs-code conflict, not merely untested.

rules.rule: assertCommentClean hard-blocks (403 REVIEW_CONTENT_BLOCKED) ANY flagged reason (phone/email/url/off_platform/address/profanity) with no partial save and no admin queue — all-or-nothing, unlike chat's flagged-but-visible posture for profanity.

A P2002 on the (reviewerId,orderId) upsert is caught and rethrown as 409 'You have already reviewed this order.' — added by BRI-831's fix; resubmitting on the happy path (no race) silently overwrites the existing row rather than erroring.

Edit/delete window is exactly 30 days from review.createdAt (assertWithinEditWindow); UpdateOrderReviewDto is deliberately narrower than create (no itemAsDescribed/shippingSpeed/communication/products) — per-product ratings can never be edited or added after order-review creation.

deleteOrderReview hard-deletes the Review row and manually deletes any pointing ReviewReport rows first (no FK, polymorphic by design) but does NOT touch any ProductReview rows the same order created.

GET /listings/:id/reviews is public, runs the page+aggregate as one $transaction (avg always matches the visible page's dataset), and returns an empty page + averageRating:0 for an unknown/deleted listingId rather than 404.
The live mobile review composer (RateReview.tsx) never sends a products array — ProductReview rows are, in practice, only ever created via direct API calls or seed data, never the shipped buyer UI.
rules.note: BRI-596, open/Backlog — GET /listings/:id/reviews and GET /sellers/me/product-reviews are both correctly built against structurally-starved data.

rules.rule: A seller can delete ANY of their own seller/product reviews with no restriction on which — a 1-star accurate unflagged review is as deletable as a policy-violating one, and the delete silently raises the seller's own rating on recompute.

replyToSellerReview enforces one reply per review, immutable, with NO content-filter/moderation check on replyText (unlike the review comment itself); the endpoint is fully built server-side (schema columns, mobile API wrapper) but has ZERO UI consumer in either app.
rules.note: BRI-98 is Canceled/'DO NOT BUILD' in Linear — the backend shipped anyway.

rules.rule: reportSellerReview/reportProductReview create a ReviewReport row but do NOT hide, flag, or otherwise alter the review itself — it stays fully visible, indistinguishable from an unreported review in every read path.

GET /admin/reviews has NO awareness of ReviewReport at all — no 'Reported' indicator, filter, or count anywhere in the response; an admin cannot tell which reviews (if any) were reported without querying the DB directly.
Admin review deletion (any admin, no ownership scoping) records no reason and sends no notification to the reviewer on any delete path (admin or seller self-delete).
Reviews are buyer-rates-seller ONLY by deliberate 27-Jul-2026 scope cut — no seller->buyer review model exists anywhere in the schema, matching BRI-66's documented resolution.

Two real past incidents (BRI-785, BRI-831) share one root cause: Review's original unique constraint was (reviewerId,sellerId) instead of (reviewerId,orderId), so a second order from the same seller silently overwrote the first review; the subsequent migration mismatch (code expected the new constraint, the real DB migration was never applied) made EVERY review submission 500 until a manual-sql fix was applied.
rules.note: The real QA database's patch status was not independently confirmed in the fix doc's own write-up — worth checking first on any QA-env 500 on review submission.

rules.rule: Mobile's order.reviewSubmitted flag (driving the 'Rate & review' CTA) is a CLIENT-ONLY optimistic flag (useOrders.getState().markReviewed) not backed by any real server field tied to the Review model.

All 4 endpoints require JwtAuthGuard at class level; markAllRead/markOneRead/deleteNotifications are all scoped to userId purely via the Prisma WHERE clause, never a prior ownership-check-then-404 — structurally impossible to touch another user's rows regardless of id/ids supplied.

markOneRead never 404s on a bad/foreign id — it silently matches zero rows and still returns {success:true}; a caller cannot distinguish 'already read', 'not yours', and 'doesn't exist' from the response alone.

DELETE is implemented as POST /notifications/delete (verb-as-path) specifically because React Native drops the request body on a DELETE verb; an empty ids array is rejected (400) by DTO validation before the service runs.
The delete response's 'deleted' count can be LESS than ids.length (some ids already gone or belonging to another user) — the one response in the module that reports partial outcomes.
No unread-count-only endpoint exists at any layer; every surface (mobile store, profile row count, inbox tab dot) computes it client-side by filtering an already-fetched up-to-100-row list.

Push is gated by a per-type preference lookup (pushPrefKeyFor); a muted push type's in-app row is STILL written (only the push itself is skipped) — the in-app notification is never conditional on a preference.

A set of ~21 notification types always send regardless of any Settings toggle (security alerts, payment failures, disputes/chargebacks, listing moderation, saved-search matches) — pushPrefKeyFor returns null for these.
sendPush never throws — both an Expo HTTP error and a network-level fetch rejection are caught and only logged; a push failure never fails the notification-creating request.

sendPush silently skips (no error/log) when there's no token or the token doesn't start with 'ExponentPushToken' — this module only refuses a token it has on file; it cannot refuse a token it was never told to forget (that's the users module's job, via DELETE /users/me/push-token).

Order-type notifications route to orderUpdates (buyer) vs sellerAlerts (seller) purely by trusting data.role stamped by the CALLER at creation time — a caller that forgets to stamp role falls through to the buyer toggle even for a seller recipient.

navigation/notificationRoute.ts (killed-app tap routing) is a SECOND, independently-maintained copy of the same per-type routing table as Notifications.tsx's openNotification — no shared table; the two must be kept in sync by hand.
REDB1-40 (the Baseline-1 copy of BRI-521) is Reopened in Linear even though the merge/preference mechanism is present and unit-tested in current code.
REDB1-69 (the Baseline-1 copy of BRI-391, conversation-dismiss) is Reopened despite dismissNotificationsForConversation existing and matching the documented fix.

POST /events is authenticated-only by deliberate design (not an oversight) — ListingEvent.userId is nullable specifically to leave room for later device-scoped guest capture without a migration, but no guest path exists today.
Write-only in this phase — nothing in apps/api/src currently queries ListingEvent for ranking; capture ships first and alone so history accumulates before scoring switches on.
202 Accepted, not 201 — events referencing a deleted listing or the submitter's own listing are deliberately dropped, so 'Created' would overpromise.

A seller's interaction with their own listing (ownListing) is dropped outright at write time, not stored-and-filtered-at-read — explicit anti-wash-trading guard; no legitimate reader would ever want that row.
No client-supplied timestamp is accepted anywhere — the server clock is the only one that counts, specifically to prevent a caller from backdating events into a favorable scoring window.
dwellMs below 1000ms is dropped (tooShort); above 120000ms (2 min) is clamped, not dropped; non-dwell events never carry a duration even if one is sent.

A batch with some bad events never throws — the whole createMany succeeds for the valid rows, since the mobile client clears its local queue on any 2xx and a full-batch failure would strand every other event in a retry loop forever.

The category is denormalised onto the event row at write time from the listing's current facets, specifically to keep the hot category-affinity scoring query off a join with Listing — a ListingEvent row survives the category's own later deletion.
A purchase event is recorded once per distinct listing in the order, never per unit — counting a 3-unit purchase as three signals would let basket size masquerade as popularity.
The mobile queue has no retry loop on a failed flush — a failed batch returns to the front of the live queue for the next natural flush, deliberately not hammered, since this is low-stakes telemetry.
Published-only filtering is server-side and unconditional — a draft article can never reach the client regardless of topic/query.
The 'shipping' topic is a keyword search, not a collection lookup, because the real Intercom workspace has no dedicated Shipping collection — several shipping articles sit outside any collection.
The full article corpus is fetched (per_page=150) on EVERY request, no server-side caching; a corpus exceeding 150 would silently fetch only page 1 and log a warning rather than paginate further.

Both endpoints are unauthenticated by design (non-user-specific content), yet BRI-338 (the feature ticket) is 'QA Testing' in Linear, not Done — implemented-and-code-verified but not yet formally closed per the tracker.
GET /health is a pure liveness check (process responds to HTTP) with ZERO dependency verification — it never pings Postgres/Redis/Qdrant/Stripe; it proves nothing about downstream service health.

POST /seed/run is additive/idempotent by construction — zero deleteMany/truncate/raw-SQL destructive calls found across all 765 lines; every one of 9 internal seed steps uses Prisma upsert keyed on a natural unique field.
The endpoint's ONLY access control is NODE_ENV!=='production' — no authentication of any kind in any non-production environment.

Seeded listings have no isSeed/isDemo flag at the schema level and no 'unseed' endpoint — seed-created data is indistinguishable from real data once created, a real environment-cleanup gap (not a safety violation).
All three endpoints order sortOrder-first, name-second, never pure alphabetical, consistently at the repository query level across all three routes and the internal cross-module methods.

Type-level images are excluded from the bulk tree response (GET /categories/tree) specifically to avoid a documented client timeout (187 types x up to 1.3MB base64 images); no endpoint exists to fetch a single type's image.
No endpoint in this module requires authentication — all taxonomy reads are public.
GET /brands orders alphabetically by name, NOT sortOrder-first — a real asymmetry with categories/materials in the same taxonomy group (no sortOrder read at all for this endpoint).
itemCount reflects only currently-live, non-deleted listings (LIVE_LISTING_WHERE) at request time, computed fresh via a Prisma _count aggregate on every call — not cached.
GET /materials is a suggestion list, not an enum enforcement — Listing.material is free text, independent of this endpoint's contents.

Mobile falls back to a built-in hardcoded list when there is neither a successful server response nor a cache yet — the Material picker must never open blank, a documented production-incident-driven safeguard.

POST /promotions/validate requires authentication (any signed-in user), is read-only (no usage-count/consumption at this endpoint), and collapses 'not found' and 'deactivated' into one identical message/path, while 'expired' is a separate distinguishable message.
Code matching is input.toUpperCase()===stored_code — a promo code must be stored in uppercase to ever match; nothing in this module's own code normalizes a lowercase-created code.
No visible mechanism in this module ties a successfully validated code to its actual application on an order total — that linkage, if it exists, lives entirely in the orders/checkout path.

GET /feed and GET /feed/followed are strictly authenticated-only by PRODUCT decision (a guest has no home-feed concept at all) — a guest hitting either gets 401 by design, not a degraded public response.
Hidden-seller exclusion (BRI-470) applies to every leg of the main feed blend (curated/scored/recent); the followed-rail needs no separate filter because hiding already implies unfollowing.

A last-resort name-derived audience lean is used ONLY in cold-start state with zero real signal, and is discarded the instant any real stated/behavioural signal exists — cannot override a real signal.
Admin feed curation (upsert-based, re-curating updates in place) and engagement-score recompute (full rebuild, never incremental) are both explicitly, deliberately safe to call repeatedly.
The admin curation/recompute endpoints (admin/feed/*) have ZERO web UI — confirmed absent by targeted search; exercisable only via direct API call today.
Only name/alertsEnabled are editable post-creation (BR33) — a filter change requires creating a new saved search, not updating the existing one; UpdateSavedSearchDto has no filter fields at all.
GET .../results computes results LIVE on every call via the exact same ListingsService.search/findMany path a direct listings call would use — never cached/precomputed.
A seller's own listing can never trigger a match notification against their own saved search — a hard SQL exclusion (userId != listing.sellerId), not a client convention.
Match notification (notifyMatches) is best-effort/non-blocking by design — a failure here must never surface as a listing-creation error to the seller.
Hard cap of exactly 10 terms per user, enforced SERVER-SIDE on every write (pruneToMostRecent runs after every record call) — not a display-only client trim.
A blank/whitespace-only term after trimming is a silent 200 no-op, NOT a validation error — a deliberate, documented asymmetry with this module's own otherwise-strict DTO type validation.
Dedup is case-insensitive by storage key (termLower unique composite with userId) but display casing always reflects the most-recently-typed variant.

City/state/ZIP combination is validated server-side as describing a real place, both on create (whole-DTO class-level validator) and on partial update (service completes the triple from the stored row before re-checking) — genuinely enforced, not merely mirrored client-side.
rules.note: BRI-263 (reopened). Corrects an earlier working hypothesis in this knowledge base's own planning notes that had flagged this as client-only.

rules.rule: The Shippo deliverability check fails OPEN on a Shippo outage/misconfiguration (logs, allows the save) but fails CLOSED (blocks with 400) when Shippo is reachable and actively reports non-deliverable.

Default-address promotion is transactional on both create and update (demote-all-others + set-new-default in one $transaction); no automatic re-promotion of another address was found on DELETE of the current default.
The public addresses/us/* routes exist specifically to support pre-session flows (seller onboarding ship-from address) and are explicitly, safely cacheable for 24h (Cache-Control header).
acceptedCities lists every city name a save will accept for a ZIP (e.g. both a borough and its parent city) — city is only the one auto-filled value, not the only one that will validate.
All three AI endpoints require a confirmed SELLER role (JwtAuthGuard+RolesGuard+@Roles('SELLER')) at class level, not merely authentication.
GET /ai/price-comps never 400s on missing tiers — it degrades gracefully to a 'not enough data' 200 response; all three tiers (category/subcategory/type) are required only for a real comparison.

analyze() and regenerate() are literally identical implementations (both call runAnalysis); the only functional difference is AiThrottlerGuard applying to analyze only — and regenerate has no live mobile UI entry point despite being fully built and tested on both ends.

checkProhibited (the typed-text defense-in-depth for 'Fill in Manually' listing creation) fails CLOSED on a prohibited-list DB lookup error (InternalServerErrorException) — the opposite fail-direction from Shippo/Intercom's fail-open pattern elsewhere in the codebase.

Five independent boolean override flags on the model's parsed response (prohibitedItemIsReplica, isProhibitedWeapon, prohibitedTermIsGraphicOnly, prohibitedThemeIsDecorative, prohibitedMentionIsIncidental) each clear a specific class of false-positive prohibited-content match; each is cited to its own prior-incident ticket.
Both embeddings endpoints share the identical environment-only access gate as seed (NODE_ENV!=='production', no other auth) — the second module in this knowledge base with this exact pattern.

backfill runs synchronously in-request (no queue); reconcile is fire-and-forget via a real BullMQ queue — a test verifying reconcile's actual effect needs a different strategy (poll worker-side state) than one verifying backfill's.
Storage is real AWS S3 (PutObjectCommand/GetObjectCommand + presigned URLs, 1h expiry) — not local disk, correcting an earlier speculative hypothesis based on main.ts's useStaticAssets line.
Every upload category's filename is a cryptographically random 96-bit token (randomBytes(12).toString('hex')) + detected extension, uniform across listings/videos/profiles/taxonomy/reviews/evidence.

Every GET .../:filename read route (listings, listing-videos, taxonomy, profiles, reviews, evidence) is unauthenticated — including dispute/refund evidence photos, which are not treated more strictly than ordinary listing photos despite plausibly higher sensitivity (could show a buyer's home/address).
rules.note: Mitigated by filename unguessability + 1h presigned-URL expiry, but no identity-based access control exists.

rules.rule: Listing-photo content type is verified by magic-byte sniffing, not trusted from the client-declared mimetype/extension — a renamed .exe/.txt is rejected, confirmed fixed from a prior real production gap.

uploadListingImages and uploadReviewImages handle zero-files and over-count-limit differently from each other (400-vs-empty-array response; custom FileCountLimitInterceptor-vs-plain maxCount for the over-limit error message) — two superficially similar multi-file endpoints, two different behaviors.
Video duration (15s cap) is enforced CLIENT-SIDE only — no server-side ffprobe-style check exists; a direct API call can upload a longer video successfully.

uploads/taxonomy, avatar, and cover have no visible explicit file-type allowlist or size-limit object on their Multer interceptor configuration, unlike listings/reviews/evidence, which all declare one.
Every one of the 56 routes requires the real Prisma Role.ADMIN enum, verified uniformly by reading the full 566-line controller — no per-route override, no exceptions found.

updateOrderStatus, resolveDispute, issueRefund, and retryPayoutReversal all converge on the same two shared chokepoints (OrdersService.applyAdminStatusChange for status/timeline/inventory-release; ConnectService.refundOrder for the actual money movement) — not four independent implementations.

deleteCategory and deleteBrand both block (409, naming the live-listing count) on a referential-integrity check; deleteSubcategory and deleteType have NO such check at all (cascading delete with no guard) — an asymmetry, unresolved whether intentional.
PATCH /admin/users/:id/role accepts the full Role enum (incl. ADMIN) with no additional confirmation step visible — any existing admin can mint new admins through this one endpoint.
GET /admin/authenticity's queue membership rule is exact: NOT_DELETED AND (status==='pending_approval' OR price>=10000 cents/$100) — a listing enters purely by price regardless of approval status.

PUT /admin/taxonomy/materials/order requires the submitted ids array to be EXACTLY the current full material-id set (same length+members); a stale client is refused outright (409), never partially applied.

deleteBrand's referential-integrity guard is load-bearing in a way deleteCategory's is not: Listing.brandId is NULLABLE at the DB level, so the application-level listing-count check is the ONLY thing preventing a brand delete from silently orphaning (nulling) every referencing listing's brand.

POST /admin/users/:id/export-data returns 202 immediately (pending history row created) with the actual gather/zip/email work done by a separate worker — same accepted-but-not-completed contract shape as POST /embeddings/reconcile.

GET /admin/users's 'deleted' status slice covers BOTH still-restorable (pending_deletion) and already-purged accounts, reading identity from the live scrubbed User row for the former and from a separate DeletedAccountArchive-style record for the latter — two genuinely different response row shapes under one status value.

The admin URL surface (admin/*) is fragmented across 5 different controllers (admin.controller.ts, disputes.controller.ts's dispute-cases, messaging.admin.controller.ts, reviews.controller.ts's admin routes, feed/curation.controller.ts) — confirmed by file location, not a defect in this module but a documentation/discoverability concern worth knowing before assuming this module's 56 endpoints are the full admin surface.

Idempotency in this codebase is two unrelated things that must never be conflated in a test scenario: (1) Stripe-operation idempotency — extensively implemented, tested, and closed for checkout, offer holds, and every Connect transfer/reversal/refund/tax-transaction call; (2) generic API-request-level idempotency (an Idempotency-Key header or platform middleware) — genuinely absent everywhere, confirmed by a zero-match grep across apps/api/src. Protection against a duplicate HTTP request is endpoint-specific, not a platform guarantee: outside the hardened checkout/offer paths, most mutating endpoints have no documented duplicate-submission protection at all.
rules.note: This entry corrects overview.md's original blanket 'the API has no idempotency keys yet' claim, which had uncritically copied apps/mobile/CLAUDE.md's framing without checking source.

rules.rule: Three dev-only operational endpoints (POST /seed/run, POST /embeddings/backfill, POST /embeddings/reconcile) share the identical access-control pattern: gated ONLY by NODE_ENV!=='production' (404 in production), with no authentication of any kind in any other environment. GET /auth/dev/otp and GET /users/me/deletion/dev-code share the same environment gate but ALSO require JwtAuthGuard (scoped to the caller's own pending code) on top of it — a stricter variant of the same pattern.
